evals.name: rich-spec-bookclub
evals.prompt: I have a project brief at sample_input_rich.md that defines the goal, scope, and user roles for a book-club companion app. Please expand it into a requirements document with user stories, user journeys, and features. Save the output as bookclub-requirements.md in the same directory.
evals.expected_output: A well-structured markdown requirements document with three roles (organizer, member, guest), user stories per role using As-a/I-want/So-that + acceptance criteria, journeys with phase tables including pain points/emotions, features that reference specific stories and journeys, and a traceability matrix.

evals.name: thin-spec-clinicflow
evals.prompt: I have a very short brief at sample_input_thin.md for a clinic appointment tool. Please expand it into user stories, user journeys, and features. Save as clinicflow-requirements.md.
evals.expected_output: A requirements document that is appropriately short given the thin input, clearly flags assumptions and gaps under Open Questions rather than inventing details, and still produces at least a handful of stories and one journey per primary role.

evals.name: ambiguous-spec-knowledgehub
evals.prompt: sample_input_ambiguous.md is an early-stage spec for an internal knowledge hub. It has unresolved design questions noted at the bottom. Expand it into a full requirements document (user stories, journeys, features). Save as knowledgehub-requirements.md.
evals.expected_output: A requirements document that acknowledges the flagged ambiguities (single-owner vs editable, reviewer criteria, refresh cadence) in its Open Questions section rather than silently picking an answer, and writes stories that are compatible with either resolution where possible.
